newsitem.title: USA: Accuser in U.S. Army sex scandal gets discharge.
newsitem.headline: Accuser in U.S. Army sex scandal gets discharge.

text.p: A female soldier whose accusations helped trigger an investigation into sexual misconduct in the U.S. Army has been granted a hardship discharge, an Army spokeswoman said Saturday.
"She requested and was granted a discharge from the Army and is now pursuing civilian life," said spokeswoman Rachel McDonald of the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground.
The soldier, Pvt. Jessica Bleckley, 18, was believed to have left the proving ground Friday, McDonald said.
McDonald said the discharge was an honourable one, and she did not know the specific reason for the hardship request or whether it was connected with the misconduct scandal.
Normally, such requests are made when personal reasons, such as an illness in the family, require a soldier's immediate attention and physical presence.
Bleckley said on a national television programme in November that she had been forced to have sex with two trainers at the proving ground.
The accusations triggered an investigation into sexual harassment and misconduct at the facility that broadened into an Army-wide probe.
Four trainers, including the two mentioned by Bleckley, at the proving ground have been formally charged and the investigation is continuing.
